paper_metadata.title: Cognitive Outcome 1 Year After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: Results From the TRACK-TBI Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, multicenter prospective design with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria (GCS 13-15, within 24h of injury). While it is a trauma-center-based sample which may limit generalizability to all mTBI, the recruitment and baseline characteristics are thoroughly described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: patients presenting to the EDs of 18 US level 1 trauma centers within 24 hours of TBI who underwent a head CT as part of routine clinical care.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as acute TBI patients at Level 1 trauma centers.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The present analysis focused on the TRACK-TBI phase 1 cohort comprising participants ≥17 years of age enrolled at the 11 then-existing sites between February 26, 2014, and May 4, 2016.
items.reasoning: Recruitment methods and the specific phase of the multicenter study are detailed.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between February 26, 2014, and May 4, 2016.
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 18 US level 1 trauma centers
items.reasoning: The clinical setting and geographic scope (US) are stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: 656 participants ≥17 years of age presenting to level 1 trauma centers within 24 hours of mTBI (Glasgow Coma Scale score 13–15)
items.reasoning: Age, GCS score, and time from injury are explicitly used as criteria.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not explicitly state the total number of eligible patients who declined participation (refusal rate) at the point of initial ED recruitment.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 3: Weighted Demographics and Medical Comorbid Conditions of Patients With mTBI, Stratified by 1-Year Cognitive Status
items.reasoning: Extensive baseline data including age, sex, race, education, and comorbidities are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is significant attrition (only 57.7% of survivors had sufficient 1-year cognitive data). However, the authors used propensity weighting to adjust for this and performed a detailed comparison between included and excluded participants, identifying systematic differences in education and race.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the phase 1 mTBI cohort who survived with at least some 1-year data (n = 1,136), 57.7% (n = 656) had sufficient cognitive outcomes data at 1 year to be included in our analysis.
items.reasoning: The completion rate for the specific cognitive battery is relatively low (57.7%), though the authors acknowledge and address this.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: A subset of indices assessed at the in-person visits could be performed by telephone when participants were unable to attend in-person visits
items.reasoning: The authors describe using telephone follow-ups to mitigate attrition for certain measures.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: (1) low-functioning individuals may not be able to perform the assessment, and (2) high-functioning individuals may have little interest in returning for follow-up assessments.
items.reasoning: The authors hypothesize reasons for loss to follow-up but do not provide specific reasons for every individual dropout.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Compared to those without sufficient cognitive outcomes data at 1 year who were excluded from the present analysis, those who were included were more likely to be White and non-Hispanic/Latino, to have more than a high school education...
items.reasoning: A clear comparison of characteristics between those included and those lost to follow-up is provided.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: those who were included were more likely to be White and non-Hispanic/Latino, to have more than a high school education
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly state that there were significant demographic differences between completers and non-completers.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (baseline clinical variables) were measured using standardized TBI Common Data Elements (CDEs) and clinical tools like the GCS and CT scans, which are reliable in acute settings.

items.evidence_snippet: enrolled patients presenting to the EDs of 18 US level 1 trauma centers within 24 hours of TBI

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: Propensity weights were derived from boosted logistic regression models predicting complete (versus noncomplete) 1-year cognitive outcome data
items.reasoning: The authors used propensity weighting for outcomes, but for missing PF data, they primarily report the counts of missingness rather than multiple imputation.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome is a composite of validated neuropsychological tests. The use of Reliable Change Indices (RCI) and demographically adjusted norms (9th percentile) provides a robust, clinically relevant definition of cognitive outcome.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Poor 1-year cognitive outcome was defined as cognitive impairment (below the ninth percentile of normative data on ≥2 cognitive tests), cognitive decline (change score... exceeding the 90% reliable change index on ≥2 cognitive tests), or both.
items.reasoning: The outcome is precisely defined with specific thresholds and timing.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The battery included 5 scores... RAVLT... Trail Making Test... Processing Speed Index... consistent with TBI Common Data Elements (CDEs).
items.reasoning: Standardized, validated neuropsychological tests were used.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Participants underwent neuropsychological testing at up to 3 in-person cognitive assessments
items.reasoning: Standardized in-person assessments were used for the cognitive battery across the cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.
